newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Novartis sees strong 97 profit growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Novartis sees strong 97 profit growth.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals and chemicals giant Novartis AG reported 1996 results in line with expectations on Tuesday, forecast strong 1997 profit growth and reassured investors that its merger was proceeding smoothly.

"In 1997, we should...experience a strong positive currency effect. Together with the realisation of the merger synthesis, this should lead, barring any unforeseen events, to a marked improvement of operating and net income," it said in a statement.
Novartis reported a 1996 group net profit of 2.304 billion Swiss francs ($1.6 billion) versus 4.216 billion in 1995. Net profit before extraordinary items was 4.175 billion after 4.096 billion.
Novartis was formed by the merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG last year. It had predicted 1996 earnings, excluding extraordinary merger-related expenses, would be about the same as in 1995.

Analysts had already discounted the results and were more eager for news on progress in integrating the two companies which were major players in the pharmaceuticals and chemicals sectors even before the merger.

Their marriage created the world's biggest pharmaceutical company after Britain's Glaxo-Wellcome. It also highlighted the sector's consolidation which has spawned giants big enough to lower costs and devote staggering sums to research and development.
Novartis said it had achieved all the goals it set for 1996 and had also seen dynamic growth in all divisions during the first two months of this year.
"This was quite in line with my estimates and with market estimates, so from that point of view it (the statement) was a non-event," said Union Bancaire Privee analyst Romain Pasche.
After divestitures, net merger-related charges were 1.9 billion francs after tax, also in line with forecasts.
Novartis pleased investors by proposing a dividend increase to 20 Swiss francs per share from 16.80, giving its shares an early boost.
It said it expected most of its integration projects to be finished this year, a statement which analysts saw as particularly positive.
"This will take some of the uncertainty out of the share (price)," said Gerd Ramsperger, head of brokerage research at Zuercher Kantonalbank.
Novartis said growth of established key products continued to be strong and new products were increasing their importance thanks to an aggressive programme of product launches.
It boosted marketing spending seven percent last year to support product launches and added to its sales force.
Analysts had been keen for information on the group's product pipeline as many of its products, particularly those inherited from Ciba-Geigy, are mature.
Executives told a news conference in London that Novartis currently had 85 pharmaceutical projects in clinical development and planned to launch 29 new products in the next three years.
By comparison, Glaxo-Wellcome is planning to launch some 20 new products within the next four years.
Novartis said last year's sales in the core "life sciences" business -- pharmaceuticals, agribusiness and nutrition -- rose eight percent to 27.60 billion francs.
Total sales including divested operations rose to 36.23 billion francs from 35.94 billion. Operating income rose four percent.
"The merger process proceeded well with limited impact on our margins, which at 20.4 percent are in line with our expectations," Financial Officer Raymund Breu said.
Group research and development (R&D) spending rose by four percent. R&D spending in the pharmaceuticals sector was maintained at 19 percent of sales.
Novartis's registered share price was down nine francs to 1,730 in mid-afternoon bourse trading. ($ = 1.459 Swiss Francs)
